title: Radioactive Decay Half-Life Explorer
learningObjectives: Define half-life as the time for half of the parent isotopes to decay and describe how remaining amount halves each interval
Apply the equation N=N0*(1/2)^(t/T) to calculate the amount remaining after a given elapsed time

sources.title: Powell Expedition—Geologic Time. Then and Now. — U.S. Geological Survey

explanations.text: Half-life describes how long it takes for half of the original parent isotopes to decay to a daughter product, leaving half the starting amount after one half-life.

evidence.quote: A half-life is the length of time it takes for half of the number of original, or parent, isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.

explanations.text: Each isotope has its own fundamental half-life value. For example, the decay of uranium-235 to lead-207 has a characteristic timescale measured in hundreds of millions of years.

evidence.quote: For example, uranium-235 is an unstable parent isotope that decays to lead-207, with a half-life of 710 million years.
It is a fundamental characteristic of a particular isotope.

explanations.text: The cake analogy illustrates exponential halving: after each half-life the remaining portion is halved again, so the amount left can be used to estimate age in number of half-lives.

evidence.quote: In this example, the half-life is one day.
On day one, you would eat half the cake and have half left (and probably go to bed with a bellyache).
